multiplechoiceresponse.p: Two reports give different numbers for "active learners". The first thing to do is:

choice.div: Check the definition of the metric and the source of truth in both.
Use the larger one, to be safe.

div.p: A disagreement between reports is nearly always a definition or pipeline difference, not two views of one truth. Trace both back to the system that owns the data.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which cleaning action is not safe to do silently?

choice.div: Deleting records you consider to be outliers.

div.p: An outlier is a question, not an error. Removing records without recording it changes the answer and hides evidence of a data problem.

choiceresponse.p: Which are sound data-governance practices? Select all that apply.

choice.div: A named owner for each critical dataset.
Keeping a data dictionary of field meanings and rules.
Copying personal data into a personal spreadsheet to work on it.
Retaining data only as long as policy requires.

div.p: Ownership, a dictionary and a retention rule are the backbone of governance. Personal data belongs in systems that are accountable for it, not in personal files.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Pseudonymising a learner ID (replacing the name with a code) does not make the data anonymous because:

choice.div: The record may still be re-identifiable by joining it with other data.

div.p: Pseudonymised data keeps a consistent key, so it can often be linked back. True anonymisation removes the ability to re-identify.
